description.short_caption: Abdominal CT scan showing intra-abdominal findings.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the abdomen demonstrates a large fluid collection with gas locules in the left upper quadrant, suggestive of an abscess. The liver and spleen are visible, with the fluid collection located adjacent to the spleen. The presence of gas within the collection suggests a possible infectious etiology. The scan is performed without visible contrast enhancement.
visible_findings: large fluid collection in the left upper quadrant
gas locules within the fluid collection

description.short_caption: Abdominal CT scan showing multiple fluid-filled structures and abnormal findings.
description.detailed_description: This axial abdominal CT scan reveals multiple fluid-filled structures, some with air-fluid levels, suggesting abscess formation or infected cysts. The scan also shows surrounding soft tissue changes, likely indicative of inflammation. The image is de-identified and includes clear visualization of abdominal organs and pathological findings.

description.short_caption: Contrast-enhanced chest CT scan showing pulmonary findings.
description.detailed_description: This is an axial view of a contrast-enhanced chest CT scan. The pulmonary vasculature is well visualized, and there are no obvious large consolidations, masses, or pleural effusions. The bronchi and lung parenchyma appear symmetric. The mediastinal structures, including the heart and great vessels, are centrally located and appear normal in size and position. The contrast enhancement highlights the vascular structures, aiding in the assessment of potential abnormalities.

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing gram-positive bacilli in peri-hepatic drainage.
description.detailed_description: This is a Gram stain image showing a background of cellular debris and scattered gram-positive bacilli, which appear as purple rod-shaped organisms against an orange-pink background. The organisms are arranged singly and in short chains. The staining technique highlights the bacterial morphology and suggests the presence of gram-positive bacteria in the peri-hepatic drainage sample.
visible_findings: bacteria arranged singly and in short chains

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing gram-positive bacilli in peri-hepatic drainage.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of a sample from peri-hepatic drainage. Numerous gram-positive bacilli, appearing as purple rod-shaped organisms, are visible against a background of pink-stained material and cellular debris. The staining highlights the bacterial morphology, with no clear clustering or spore formation evident. The image suggests a bacterial infection involving gram-positive organisms.

description.short_caption: 12-lead ECG showing electrical activity of the heart.
description.detailed_description: This is a 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) tracing showing the electrical activity of the heart. The leads are labeled as I, II, III, aVR, aVL, aVF, and V1-V6. The tracing shows regular rhythm with visible P waves, QRS complexes, and T waves. Measurements such as heart rate, PR interval, QRS duration, and QTc are listed at the top of the image. The ECG grid provides a standard format for analyzing the waveform morphology and intervals.
visible_findings: visible P waves, QRS complexes, and T waves
measurement data at the top of the image

description.short_caption: Abdominal CT scan showing a large hypodense lesion in the liver.
description.detailed_description: This axial abdominal CT scan reveals a large, well-defined hypodense lesion in the liver, suggestive of an abscess or cyst. Adjacent bowel loops and other abdominal structures are visible, with no clear evidence of bowel obstruction. The scan appears to be performed without intravenous contrast, as there is no enhancement of vascular structures or the lesion. The vertebral body and paraspinal structures are also partially visible.
visible_findings: large hypodense lesion in the liver
vertebral body and paraspinal structures partially visible
